observation.visible_scene: A glass lensball rests on a wet, pebbly shoreline in the left foreground while the sun sits low on the horizon over calm water. The sky is orange-pink with a few clouds, a thin strip of distant land marks the horizon, and a bright vertical glare path from the sun reflects on the water to the right. Inside the ball an inverted, refracted image of the same sunset scene (including the sun's glare as a bright streak on the ball's left side) is visible.
visible_changes: The ball and the pebbles beneath it stay in the same pixel positions across all frames; no translation or rotation of the ball is visible.
The thin film of water and small ripples around the pebbles and at the ball's base undulate and shift shape continuously from frame to frame (an ongoing lapping motion, not a start or stop).
The sun's reflection column on the open water shimmers and breaks into moving segments as the surface ripples change.
The refracted image inside the ball shows minor brightness/shape variations of the inverted glare streak, tracking the changing water surface rather than indicating a separate object.
The horizon line, sky, and cloud positions remain essentially fixed, indicating no noticeable camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the overall water level is rising or falling (tide direction) is not determinable from this short excerpt.
The cause of the surface ripples (wind, current, etc.) is not visible.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67 s are unknown.
uncertain_details: Any sub-pixel wobble of the ball on the pebbles is too small to confirm.
The exact advance/retreat direction of the waterline between successive frames is ambiguous due to the gentle, oscillating nature of the ripples.
The bright vertical line inside the ball is a refracted reflection of the sun's water glare, not a separate physical object; this interpretation is consistent but inferred from optics.
